docker_image_upgrades.description: Standard upgrade path for all OpenDataRemoval Docker images
docker_image_upgrades.frequency: Monthly or when security advisories affect base images

steps.action: Take a backup before any upgrade
steps.command: cd /home/{deploy_user}/opendataremoval && ./scripts/backup.sh

steps.action: Pull latest images
steps.command: docker compose pull

steps.action: Check if DB migrations are needed (only required when api image changes)
steps.command: docker compose run --rm api alembic current
steps.note: If output shows 'head' already, no migration needed. If behind, see migration_guide below.

steps.action: Apply migrations if needed
steps.command: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head

steps.action: Recreate containers with new images
steps.command: docker compose up -d --force-recreate

steps.action: Verify health
steps.command: sleep 15 && curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/system/health | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('STATUS:', d['data']['status'])"

steps.action: Verify frontend loads and shows correct version
steps.method: Open dashboard, check browser console for errors

rollback.description: If upgrade causes issues, roll back to previous image tags
steps: Pin specific image versions in docker-compose.yml (e.g. postgres:15.6-alpine instead of postgres:15-alpine)
docker compose up -d --force-recreate
If DB migration was applied: docker compose run --rm api alembic downgrade -1

alembic_migration_guide.description: How to create and apply database schema migrations when the data model changes
alembic_migration_guide.check_current_version: docker compose run --rm api alembic current
alembic_migration_guide.check_pending: docker compose run --rm api alembic history --indicate-current
alembic_migration_guide.apply_migrations: docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
alembic_migration_guide.rollback_one: docker compose run --rm api alembic downgrade -1
alembic_migration_guide.rollback_to_base: docker compose run --rm api alembic downgrade base

create_new_migration.auto_generate: docker compose run --rm api alembic revision --autogenerate -m 'description_of_change'
create_new_migration.manual: docker compose run --rm api alembic revision -m 'description_of_change'
create_new_migration.location: Generated in migrations/versions/ — review before applying
create_new_migration.warning: Always review auto-generated migrations — autogenerate may miss encrypted column changes

migration_with_backup.description: Safe procedure for applying migrations in production
steps: 1. Take full backup: ./scripts/backup.sh
2. docker compose stop api worker beat playwright mailwatcher
3. docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head
4. docker compose start api worker beat playwright mailwatcher
5. Verify: curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/system/health
1. docker compose run --rm api pip list --outdated > /tmp/outdated.txt && cat /tmp/outdated.txt
2. Update specific packages in api/requirements.txt, mailwatcher/requirements.txt, or playwright/requirements.txt
3. Rebuild affected images: docker compose build api (or mailwatcher/playwright)
4. docker compose up -d
5. Run test suite: cd /home/{deploy_user}/opendataremoval && pytest tests/unit/ -v
6. Check health
python_dependency_updates.caution: Playwright version in playwright/requirements.txt must match the Chromium version installed in the Dockerfile. Update both together.

steps: 1. Backup n8n workflows: docker compose exec n8n n8n export:workflow --all --output=/home/node/.n8n/workflows/
2. docker compose pull n8n
3. docker compose up -d n8n
4. Verify n8n UI loads at :5678
5. Verify workflows are present and active
n8n_upgrade.note: n8n workflow format occasionally changes between major versions. Check n8n release notes before pulling 'latest' across major versions.

playbook_updates.description: Updating broker automation playbooks when broker sites change their opt-out flow
steps: 1. Identify the changed broker from dashboard action items or failed scan notifications
2. Edit playbooks/brokers/{canonical_domain}.json
3. Increment playbook_version field
4. Validate: python3 -c "import json, jsonschema; jsonschema.validate(json.load(open('playbooks/brokers/{domain}.json')), json.load(open('playbooks/schema.json'))); print('Valid')"
5. Import via seed script: docker compose run --rm api python scripts/seed_brokers.py --domain {canonical_domain}
6. Test with dry run: POST /api/scans {broker_id, profile_id, dry_run: true} from dashboard
7. Review dry run screenshots
8. If satisfied, trigger live scan for this broker

symptom_scan_errors.title: Scan results mostly error or inconclusive

steps.command: docker compose exec api curl -s http://playwright:8001/health
steps.if_fail: docker compose restart playwright && sleep 10 && docker compose exec api curl -s http://playwright:8001/health

steps.check: Check Playwright logs for Chromium errors
steps.command: docker compose logs playwright --tail=100 | grep -i 'error\|chromium\|crash'
steps.common_cause: Shared memory exhaustion — check shm_size: 256mb is set in docker-compose.yml

steps.check: Is the host IP being blocked? (rate limiting)
steps.command: docker compose logs playwright --tail=100 | grep -i 'rate_limited\|429\|too many'
steps.if_yes: Increase PLAYWRIGHT_MIN_DELAY_MS and PLAYWRIGHT_MAX_DELAY_MS in .env. Consider enabling PLAYWRIGHT_PROXY_URL.

steps.method: Check scan_results table for which specific brokers are erroring
steps.command: docker compose exec db psql -U opendataremoval opendataremoval -c "SELECT b.canonical_domain, sr.result_status, sr.error_message FROM scanning.scan_results sr JOIN registry.brokers b ON sr.broker_id=b.id WHERE sr.result_status='error' AND sr.scanned_at > now() - interval '1 day' ORDER BY sr.scanned_at DESC LIMIT 20;"
steps.action: Update playbooks for repeatedly failing brokers — see upgrade_procedures.playbook_updates

symptom_captcha_flood.title: CAPTCHA blocked appearing on many brokers

steps.action: Increase scan delays temporarily
steps: Update PLAYWRIGHT_MIN_DELAY_MS=5000 and PLAYWRIGHT_MAX_DELAY_MS=10000 in .env
docker compose restart worker playwright

steps.action: Enable proxy rotation (long-term fix)
steps: Set PLAYWRIGHT_PROXY_URL in .env to a residential proxy or Tor endpoint
docker compose restart worker playwright
Verify: docker compose logs playwright | grep proxy

symptom_worker_backlog.title: Worker queue growing without being processed

steps.command: docker compose exec redis redis-cli -a $REDIS_PASSWORD LLEN celery
docker compose exec worker celery -A workers.celery_app inspect active
docker compose exec worker celery -A workers.celery_app inspect reserved

steps.command: docker compose exec worker celery -A workers.celery_app purge

symptom_encryption_key.title: PII not decrypting — 500 errors on profile endpoints
symptom_encryption_key.likely_cause: DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY in .env does not match the key used to encrypt the data

steps.command: grep DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY .env | wc -c
docker compose exec db psql -U opendataremoval opendataremoval -c "SELECT pgp_sym_decrypt(display_name::bytea, current_setting('app.encryption_key')) FROM identity.profiles LIMIT 1;"
steps.if_error: Key mismatch — restore .env from GPG backup: gpg --decrypt ~/opendataremoval-secrets-backup.gpg | grep DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY

steps.action: Restore DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY from GPG backup. The data cannot be recovered without the original key.

steps.warning: If original key is permanently lost, all PII is unrecoverable. Profiles must be deleted and re-entered.

steps.check: N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET matches in both .env and n8n environment
steps.command: grep N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET .env && docker compose exec n8n env | grep N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET

steps.if_mismatch: Update N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env to match, or restart n8n to pick up the current .env value: docker compose restart api n8n

steps.check: n8n Code node computing HMAC correctly
steps.method: In n8n UI, open Compute HMAC Signature node, click Execute node with test data, verify signature format is sha256={hex}

steps: Dashboard → Settings → Profiles → Add Profile
Enter full legal name, date of birth
Add all known addresses (current and previous 2 years)
Add all phone numbers (current and recent)
Add all email addresses (current and any used in past 5 years)
Add any known aliases or maiden names
Save — system will automatically schedule a full scan for the new profile within 24 hours
Dashboard → Settings → Profiles → select member → Edit
Toggle 'Pause automation' to ON
Save — all scans and removal actions suspended, data retained
Dashboard → Broker Registry → search for broker
Click broker → View requests for this broker
If no active request: Dashboard → Scans → Trigger manual scan for specific profile + broker
If exposure found: removal request will be auto-created
If request already exists and is stuck: Request Tracker → find request → Resubmit
Create playbooks/brokers/{canonical_domain}.json following DOC-6 schema
Validate: python3 -c "import json,jsonschema; jsonschema.validate(json.load(open('playbooks/brokers/{domain}.json')), json.load(open('playbooks/schema.json')))"
Import: docker compose run --rm api python scripts/seed_brokers.py --domain {canonical_domain}
Verify in Dashboard → Broker Registry

pause_all_automation.description: Stop all scanning and removal activity temporarily (e.g. during maintenance)
steps: docker compose stop worker beat
Note: Mailwatcher continues to classify incoming emails (harmless)
Note: n8n discovery continues (harmless)
To resume: docker compose start worker beat
Dashboard → Reports → Audit Log
Filter by event_type=removal_email_sent or removal_submitted
Filter by broker name
Click row to see detail JSON including email subject, form fields submitted
